relevance_note: Case series of three ATS families with SLC2A10 genotypes plus a summary table of the authors' earlier ATS patients: "In Patient 1 (Family A), sequencing analysis revealed the homozygous c.1309G>A transition".
method_note: Read the whole paper including both supplementary tables; built the JSON with a Python script in my scratch directory from hand-chosen values; spans for Table 1 and Supplementary Table 2 are row prefixes cut by the script from the table lines and every span was checked verbatim against the paper. Scope: Patients 1-4 (Families A-C) first-hand; tested heterozygous parents (two per family, sex not stated, so 'parent of ...') and the heterozygous fetus of Family C's second pregnancy; the eight previously reported patients of the authors' cohort shown only as columns 5-12 of Supplementary Table 2 (labels 'Table S2 column k', k counting data columns from the left: 1-4 = Patients 1-4, 5 = Family D, 6 = E, 7 = F, 8 = G, 9-12 = the four Family H members; per-patient references taken from the header superscripts and the legend); and four previously published people mentioned in the Discussion with an individual fact (ref [8] Italian compound-heterozygous carrier of c.1309G>A, two Callewaert [5] patients: death at 33 y and stroke at 8 months, Allen [41] 27-year-old woman). Possible duplicates not merged: 'ref [8] patient' may be Table S2 column 8 (Family G cites [8]); the two 'ref [5]' people may be one person. Left out: Patient 1's unaffected older brother and the elder healthy brother in Family B (neither stated as tested nor affected; 'Segregation was verified in all families' names no one); the 3 of 4 cohort women with pregnancies (counts only). Patient 4 was not genotyped (only his parents were), so he has no variant row. No variant rows for Table S2 columns 5-12: the paper never attributes a specific variant to them (Table S1 lists variants by reference, not by patient). Variant inheritance left 'not reported' for the homozygous probands: both parents are stated heterozygous carriers (quoted in parental_testing_statement), but the enum has no biparental value. Transcript NM_030777.3 comes from the Methods statement that applies to all variants. Table symbols: neither Table 1 nor Table S2 defines '-' as absent, so '-' cells were treated as not reported (no excluded rows from them); '+' cells were taken as present. Excluded rows come only from text: Patient 1 'absence of joint hypermobility ... (0/9)', Patient 2 'systolic pulmonary artery pressure was normal' (excluded elevated pulmonary pressure / pulmonary hypertension), normal psychomotor development (P1-P3), and arterial dissection for all 12 cohort patients from the group statement 'dissections did not occur' about 'our cohort' of 12. Vital status 'alive' for the 11 surviving cohort patients from 'Eleven patients ... are still alive' plus 'One patient died at 26 months'. Age at last evaluation for Table S2 columns 5-12 is the 'Sex/age on examination' cell; the 'Present age' row (bare numbers, later) was not used for it. RV hypertension was not counted as pulmonary hypertension on the checklist; Table S2 'Dyspnea/cyanosis' was not counted as respiratory distress. Discrepancies inside the paper (recorded the positive statements, none treated as excluded because '-' is undefined): Patient 1 stenting of PA at 8 years (text) vs at 2 years (Table 1); Patient 1 high-arched palate '-' in Table 1 but present in text and Table S2; Patient 1 uvula abnormalities '+' in Table 1 but '-' in Table S2; Patient 1 'absence of joint hypermobility' while 'patella hyperlaxity' is reported; Patients 2 and 3 scaphocephaly '-' in Table 1 but 'mild scaphocephaly' in the Figure 2 legend; Patients 2 and 3 hyperextensible '-' in Table 1 but '+' in Table S2 and 'poorly hyperextensible' in text; Patients 2 and 3 beaked nose '+' in Table 1 but '-' in Table S2; Patient 2 uvula 'bifid' (Table 1) vs 'elongated uvula with median raphe' (text), both recorded; Patient 3 atrophic scars '-' in Table 1 but present in text; Patient 4 onset 'First months' (Table 1) vs '2 m' (Table S2); Patient 1 is 14 years in the text but Table S2 'Present age' 16; Family D 'Aortic aneurysm +' in Table S2 while the text calls her aneurysm a small splenic artery aneurysm (both recorded; aortic root aneurysm checklist not reported); the text's ascending vs aortic root aneurysm in two Family H members ('respectively') cannot be assigned to columns 9 and 10, so aortic root aneurysm is not reported for them, and the valve-sparing aortic root replacement 'in the patient of family H at 19 years of age' was not attributed to a column (only the Surgery '+' cell for column 9 is recorded). Patient 4 is not called a proband, so is_proband is null. n_patients_reported = 4 (the four new patients; Patient 4 was not genotyped); cohort_size_as_stated = 12.
